approval: User explicitly requested API comparison and statistical correlation; bounded new NLL comparison, separate from completed historical $1 style-search sequence. No top-up.
selection: 10 uniformly sampled articles per NLL decile, plus all lowest 10. Primary inference uses only the 100 stratified articles; extra lowest-NLL anchors are descriptive.
primary: Two-sided Spearman rho: Qwen mean token NLL versus word-count-weighted Pangram window class_probabilities[2]. Negative means lower NLL aligns with higher detector score. Derived segment-score mean is not a calibrated document probability.
ci: 95% percentile bootstrap resampling within NLL deciles
secondary: primary score after excluding windows under 20 API words
lowest_comparison: Descriptive only; do not add anchor oversample to primary inferential sample.
limitations: Exploratory association within these 1000 Wikipedia transcripts; not causal and not a whole-Wikipedia false-positive estimate.
Template-stripping artifacts retained unchanged to match NLL-scored text. Missing-value regex and linebreak flags frozen before API results.
Rounded/underflowed probabilities create ties; API scores need not be calibrated.
Articles may share census boilerplate; article-wise inference assumes independent articles and does not prove independent prose templates.
Only primary p-value determines statistical significance; secondary analyses exploratory.
No additional scans or sample-size increases after observing results.

rubric.status: Consulted; no stylistic resemblance judgment or rubric-based selection. All style dimensions unassessed; objective NLL selection authorized by user.
